text:
lol, I love the “he evolved” argument. 

“My paramount object in this struggle is to save the Union, and is not either to save or to destroy slavery. If I could save the Union without freeing any slave I would do it, and if I could save it by freeing all the slaves I would do it; and if I could save it by freeing some and leaving others alone I would also do that. What I do about slavery, and the colored race, I do because I believe it helps to save the Union; and what I forbear, I forbear because I do not believe it would help to save the Union." 
~ Abraham Lincoln, The Collected Works of Abraham Lincoln, Volume V, "Letter to Horace Greeley" (August 22, 1862), p. 388.

“The original proclamation has no constitutional or legal justification, except as a military measure. The exemptions were made because the military necessity did not apply to the exempted localities. Nor does that necessity apply to them now any more than it did then. If I take the step must I not do so, without the argument of military necessity…”
~ Lincoln in a letter to Salmon Chase, Sep 2, 1863

“The most that can be said of so much, is that slaves are property. Is there, has there ever been, any question that by the law of war, property, both of enemies and friends, may be taken when need? 
~ Abraham Lincoln to James Conkling (Roy P. Basler, editor, The Collected Works of Abraham Lincoln, Volume VI, p. 406-410 (Letter to James C. Conkling, August 26, 1863)

On Aug. 17, 1864, Lincoln drafted a letter to a Wisconsin newspaper editor who had previously supported the administration, but who said he could no longer do so if the president insisted on abolition. Lincoln wrote: “To me it seems plain that saying re-union and abandonment of slavery would be considered, if offered, is not saying that nothing else or less would be considered. If Jefferson Davis wishes … to know what I would do if he were to offer peace and re-union, saying nothing about slavery, let him try me.”

“My enemies say I am now carrying on this war for the sole purpose of abolition. It is and will be carried on so long as I am President for the sole purpose of restoring the Union. But no human power can subdue this rebellion without using the Emancipation lever as I have done.”
~ Abraham Lincoln, Interview with Alexander W. Randall and Joseph T. Mills (19 Aug 1864)

What year did he evolve again?

text:
Anti-Data Centers Is The New Nuclear Freeze: China Wants To End American AI Dominance, Energy Production And Everything Else https://t.co/Ou7VM2cE46 @realDonaldTrump @SpeakerJohnson @LeaderJohnThune @RepJeffries @SenSchumer 

By Robert Romano

“I would hate to see China win the war on AI... I have a sense that China is funding the opposition to AI [data] centers.”

That was  @SenRonJohnson  (R-Wis.) in a Breitbart News interview on Aug. 31 https://t.co/SdTMC5cP5I warning that the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) might be funding opposition to data centers — more than 5,400 nationwide according to Cloudscene https://t.co/QlPk1dRplV — utilized by artificial intelligence (AI) and other internet companies to store and process large amounts of data used every day on our smart phones, computers and by large critical infrastructure including financial, educational, communications, entertainment, medical, military, emergency dispatch and other government institutions, and utilities, water management and the power grid.

Just about everything we do today runs on data — and it runs on electricity, a lot of it. And to keep America’s distinct advantage globally, we need to build more of it. A lot more of it.

And China knows it. According to an estimate by cyber security firm Alethea, China, Russia and other foreign adversaries have been actively promoting anti-data center propaganda on state media, with social media bots providing echo chambers: “The most attributable layer is overt state media, which is already running at full steam. The message pushed by Russia, China, and Iran largely converges around the idea that America is hoarding power and water for the elites while ordinary people suffer, with each country tailoring messaging to their respective geopolitical interests and domestic audiences…” https://t.co/rbeJKK2mog

There are several propaganda pieces promoting increasing electricity prices, China’s AI buildout succeeding while the U.S. fails and local opposition to data centers: “What domestic actors seed and foreign-linked networks amplify, the AI slop machine scales, producing a volume of emotionally resonant, locally targeted content that is difficult to attribute, harder to counter, and arrives faster than comms teams can respond.”

If this all sounds familiar, it should.

It's the modern-day nuclear freeze movement. In the Cold War, State Department analyses show the Soviets actively funded fronts like the World Peace Council to stoke fears of the dangers of nuclear war and to push for unilateral disarmament. https://t.co/tyEd3gbE5g

Well, it was a bad idea then, and it’s a bad idea now. The KGB did not invent American fear of the bomb, but it did exploit it. The same thing is happening today.

The need to build out technology, energy and mineral infrastructure including rare earths lies at the heart of President Donald Trump’s plan to protect our economic and national security. And today's opposition is just as dangerous as it was in the 1980s.

In May, Treasury @SecScottBessent, speaking at 2026 Reagan Economic Forum in Simi Valley, Calif. warned of the danger: “Somewhere along the way, we lost sight of a foundational principle that previous generations understood instinctively: economic security is national security, for a nation that cannot manufacture, mine, ship, or refine its needs gradually cedes its strength—and sovereignty—to others. That is a dangerous dependency for any country. It is an unacceptable one for the United States.” https://t.co/01VRpwgYoB

Bessent added, “[S]ecure supply chains matter as much as stock indices. That productive capacity is power. That trade policy, industrial policy, and national security policy must all fit together, or they will each fail separately.” He’s right.

If we get into a world war with China or Russia we might lack the manufacturing capacity to keep up with producing planes, tanks, bombs, ships, missiles, drones, etc. because of decades of outsourcing that is still being reversed.

In 10 or 15 years, such a conflict might be AI-driven, with automated weapons systems, and the country with the most compute and the most electricity — and who could keep those systems running amid a vast assault — would be the power that wins. It is not hard to imagine a contest pitting one nation’s artificial general intelligence versus another’s.

China is already pre-positioning inside U.S. energy, water, and communications networks to conduct more cyberattacks, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency reports. https://t.co/MCvhucP6qe In an actual shooting war, it will be much worse.

To compete — and to deter threats — to borrow a phrase from Captain Kirk: We need more power.

At a Potterville, Mich. Rally in August 2024, President Donald Trump warned that the U.S. needs to double electricity output to compete with China on AI, stating “For us to compete successfully with China and others on AI, we’re going to need twice the electricity that we currently produce. Can you believe that? We’re not going to be even close. The only guy that can do that is a guy like me.” https://t.co/wqLH52m9RM

But electricity output increased by 2.8 percent in 2025, from 4.308 trillion kilowatthours in 2024 to 4.429 trillion kilowatthours (kWh), according to the latest data compiled by the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA). https://t.co/ViDZdBu2SD At that pace, it will take more than two decades to double the grid.

Tech companies including xAI, Meta, Amazon, Oracle and others are already increasing electricity generation on site, https://t.co/eZh8NPrAon but the bigger projects could still be a few years off — and we’re still nowhere close to the President’s goal. We’ve got a long way to go.

Besides how long it takes to get new power stations online, one reason for the slow growth of America’s grid is because of lawsuits against America’s electric and other energy producers. On June 25, 2025, @SenTedCruz  (R-Texas) chaired a hearing https://t.co/hpHyVfbhmO at the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Federal Courts, Oversight, Agency Action, and Federal Rights entitled, “Enter the Dragon—China and the Left’s Lawfare Against American Energy Dominance.”

At the hearing, Cruz laid out the scheme, alleging, “There is a coordinated assault by the radical left, backed and paid for by the Chinese Communist Party to seize control of our courts, to weaponize litigation against U.S. energy producers. All in order to undermine American energy dominance. At stake, is a lot more than an industry. Our energy sector is the engine of American prosperity, the lifeblood of our industrial power, our national security, and our geopolitical leverage…. [F]oreign money from entities tied to the Chinese Communist Party flows into the United States to bankroll climate advocacy groups who litigate against American Energy… [A]ctivist lawyers flood our courts with lawsuits designed not to win policy debates but to bankrupt energy producers and to dismantle energy infrastructure through sheer attrition.” https://t.co/eBuWpUB2Tx

This is not the first time Beijing has meddled in the U.S. legal system. A Nov. 2023 Bloomberg News report by Emily Siegel, “China Firm Funds U.S. Suits Amid Push to Disclose Foreign Ties” found China-backed firms funding litigation in U.S. patent courts. https://t.co/uUlrfBqS4h

To address the threat of foreign influence in American courts undermining economic and national security, Congressional Republicans have offered vital legislation. The Protecting Our Courts from Foreign Manipulation Act,  H.R. 2675, https://t.co/eRp3Qsrd5d by U.S. @RepBenCline  (R-Va.), would prohibit or require disclosure of certain foreign-backed litigation funding arrangements. And the Litigation Transparency Act, H.R. 1109, https://t.co/RSqwpqNd4X by U.S. @repdarrellissa  (R-Calif.) would require parties in federal civil cases to disclose when outside financiers have a financial stake in litigation.

In addition, President Trump could issue executive orders under the Corporate Transparency Act for the Treasury Department to designate litigation funders as entities required to report their beneficial owners and under the Bank Secrecy Act to trigger additional reporting requirements.

To reach President Trump’s goal of doubling electricity output and remaining number one in technology including AI, we need all-of-the-above — whatever it takes, get more coal, nuclear, solar and everything else that has capacity to grow. In the meantime, China is able to exponentially expand, uses subsidies freely and without the federal, state and local barriers we artificially put in our own way — while Congress has appeared reluctant to subsidize at the levels that might be necessary to compete long term. America’s industrial policy along with its grid needs a substantial upgrade.

Hopefully, it will not take an emergency like Pearl Harbor to again awaken a sleeping giant. Peace through strength means that to secure peace, we must prepare for war. In so doing, we deter the next Pearl Harbor, the next 9/11.

text:
I have spent hundreds of millions of dollars on marketing ($100+ million/year at times and mostly on advertising). I know a bit about this topic. Viewer count is an important consideration. However, who they are (and where they are) matters a lot as well. Notre Dame offers the advantage of scarcity. Advertisers can reach large numbers of Southern and SEC fans through many teams and many conference broadcasts. There is only one Notre Dame. Its audience includes pockets of loyal viewers in New York, Chicago, Philadelphia, Boston, LA and numerous other markets—people who may not ordinarily watch an LSU–Mississippi State type of game. That can make a Notre Dame viewer more valuable to a national advertiser because the telecast may provide:
-Greater geographic diversity.
- Better penetration of major Northern and Midwestern markets.
- Less duplication with the rest of an advertiser’s SEC-heavy football schedule.
- A distinctive combination of sports loyalty, academic affiliation and Catholic cultural identification.
- Potentially attractive income and educational demographics.
LSU’s advantage is different: concentration and intensity. If an advertiser wants to sell pickup trucks, beer, mobile service, fast food, home-improvement products or financial services in Louisiana and surrounding states, LSU may be the better property. Its audience is not merely watching a football team; for many viewers, LSU represents the state itself. That can produce unusually strong attention, emotional engagement and advertising recall. LSU also benefits from the SEC ecosystem. A major LSU game attracts not only LSU supporters but supporters of the opponent and fans across the conference who care about the result. In a marquee matchup, that SEC multiplier can overwhelm Notre Dame’s normal national-audience advantage. 
Notre Dame sells breadth, national portability and a hard-to-replicate audience. LSU sells depth, regional dominance and the deep engagement of the SEC audience. For a national brand trying to reach consumers across the country, particularly outside the Southeast, a Notre Dame audience is more attractive than an equally sized LSU audience. For a mass-market advertiser heavily exposed to the South—or for a truly marquee SEC game—LSU may be equally or more attractive. The correct valuation depends not just on total viewers, but on geography, age, income, incremental reach, audience duplication and the particular opponent.

1) We are all the offspring of God, including the angels in Heaven. As such, we are spiritually brothers and sisters. Since Christ is the offspring of God, as is Lucifer (a personage of spirit), the familiar relationship is there. Thus the fall of Lucifer is tragic, as well as just, for he rebelled against God.

2) Actually, Kolob comes from the Book of Abraham, who called it the "Residence of God." While this teaching  is not a core part of LDS doctrine, it is an interesting piece of trivia. One I've never heard brought up in church meetings, other than the hymn, tbh.

3) That is not official Church doctrine. Members, as well as any other person, can believe what they will. I seriously doubt that Christ will condemn someone for such a belief.

4) Such is also not official Church doctrine and is not taught. Note, that we are to follow Christ’s example, and imitate His way of life. As an adjunct to the previous sentence, is it reasonable to conclude that perhaps He and the Father both have an eternal companion, thereby providing yet another example for the Children of God to follow?
Personally, I have no opinion on the matter and it was never taught to me in Church, during missionary training, or leadership training. I figure we’ll all find out the answer in due time.

5) Yes, Joseph Smith did receive revelation that the Garden of Eden would have been in the area of the USA that we now call Missouri. Many other Christian sects believe it to have been in what is now modern-day Turkey. In both cases there no archeological evidence to back up either claim, and must therefore be a matter of faith. I’ll go with Brother Joseph on this one as I have a testimony of his being called of God as a Prophet.

6) You’d need to define what you mean by “real Christians.” Anyone who believes in Christ as the Only Begotten Son of God the Father is a Christian, but Christ alone is the true judge of who His followers are.
Beyond that it is a matter of faith in revealed doctrine, including OT and NT, as well as the Book of Mormon and other latter-day revelation.
If you mean that we claim to be the restored Church, of the same organization as in New Testament times, prior to the apostasy (or removal of God’s authority to administer and minister in His kingdom) then, yes, that’s our assertion.

In no way does that mean that I feel free to point fingers at other Christians and tell them they are going to Hell. In fact, the LDS Church offers to add the additional testimony of modern revelation and the Book of Mormon as an extension of Gospel truths that were previously lost due to the apostasy. Bring what you know of Christ and allow us to add to that.

7) Incorrect. From 1852 to 1978 Blacks, to use the term your “source” uses, were indeed barred from certain temple ceremonies. There was no banishment from Heaven. For what reasons? I can only speculate, but am willing to await further revelation on the matter or until Christ addresses it, during His Millennial Reign.

8) Not exactly in the way that this statement makes it sound. No dead bodies are placed into a baptismal font. Instead, baptisms for the dead are performed by living proxies, on behalf of deceased loved ones, as well as strangers. Paul addresses this practice in 1 Corinthians 15:29.
There is contemporary historical evidence for this practice, see the Marcionites, and Cerinthians. It was banned by the Synod of Hippo in 393AD. So, nearly 400 years of the practice was removed by those who did not have the authority to act in God’s name.
As LDS Doctrine holds a core belief that God provided a way for us to have eternal families, including our long deceased ancestors, and since it is unjust to condemn those of His children who never heard the name of Christ in their lifetimes, the practice of baptism for the dead makes a lot of sense.

9) Guilty! As exalted beings, perfected in Christ after the remission of our sins, we are to become joint heirs with Christ. In other words, we are to become like him. I think much of the problems that people have with this doctrine is in their personal understanding or misunderstanding of what that means.  Thus, modern-day prophets are needed to help us better understand as they teach us and also call us to repentance as they testify of Christ.

10) Not official doctrine, and more of individual speculation of what it means to be an exalted being. While I think it would be neat, I will await Judgement and see what else the Lord reveals.

11) “magic underwear”…sorry, I find that funny after all these years of hearing that one. The sacred garments are worn to remind us of our temple covenants with God. Note, other early Christian sects also wore similar clothing.
For each individual who wears them, it is between them and God as to reasons for removal. They can be measures of protection, and I know of many instances where this was true, but which are not my stories to tell. The Church does provide recommended guidance, but no one is taking notes of our personal habits.

12) Categorically false. The Word of Wisdom admonishes us to refrain from “hot drinks” (traditionally coffee and tea), alcohol, and tobacco. We are also instructed to eat wholesome foods, including grains and both fruits and vegetables in their seasons. We are not to overly consume meat. It is a revealed code for good health, and I appreciate it.

If you want to exchange name calling, I could resort to doing so. Lemming comes to mind and also willfully ignorant. However, I shall not apply either to you, and will hold my peace as to the degree I believe them to be accurate descriptors of yourself.

Instead, I will close with this:

God Lives. Jesus IS the Christ. And God has again called prophets in these latter-days, to preach repentance until His children.

Until we meet at the Judgement Bar of Christ, as I will not continue this conversation. I prefer to avoid the spirit of contention, where I can.

2026 Hunting Forecast: North-central Montana Big Game Forecast (Region 4)

GREAT FALLS – Big game species across most of FWP's Region 4 came out of the 2025–26 winter in good condition, with strong overwinter survival rates for not only adults but also the fawns and calves born in 2025. During the winter and spring much of the region experienced a continuance of the moderate to severe drought that reduced habitat quality, but timely and abundant rainfall in late spring and early summer rapidly and significantly improved forage and overall habitat conditions. As a result, elk, deer and pronghorn are entering the critical fall and winter period of 2026 in very good body condition for the first time in the past several years. This turnaround gives wildlife managers optimism, and barring a particularly harsh winter, they anticipate strong fawn and calf production next year – setting the stage for improved hunter success and big game populations in the seasons ahead.

Access in Region 4 consists of large areas of state and federal land that provide big game hunting opportunities that are open to everyone, although hunters who are willing to hike away from roads and access points and concentrate on less accessible terrain generally have better chances of locating animals. Region 4 also has well over a million acres of private land enrolled in the state's Block Management Program, which allows public access to private land. Other private lands may also offer some hunting access, especially to hunters willing to harvest antlerless animals. As always, hunters should contact landowners well in advance of the season to secure hunting permission.

Elk

Elk numbers in Region 4 are very strong and generally meet or exceed population objectives in all districts, but the distribution of elk on the landscape varies widely. Many elk concentrate in large numbers on private lands which offer limited or no public access, while nearby public lands may hold relatively few animals.

Access to private-land elk hunting in Region 4 varies considerably, both among districts and among individual landowners. Some landowners allow hunting only for antlerless elk, while others permit either-sex harvest. Opportunities to hunt bulls differs widely depending upon the district, and in many districts, hunters with a general elk license may pursue bulls. But in several districts, especially island mountain ranges, the Missouri River Breaks and certain state-owned wildlife management areas bull hunting is limited to hunters who drew a limited entry permit.

Several hunting districts in Region 4 have shoulder seasons, which offer hunting for antlerless elk outside of the general archery and rifle seasons. Hunters should read their regulations carefully before hunting, and consider taking advantage of these special opportunities to harvest antlerless elk.

Mule Deer

Hunters can expect to find that mule deer numbers will vary widely across Region 4 this year, due in large part to the great diversity of landscape and habitat types found in the region. In some areas, especially those with substantial agricultural ground, hunters can expect moderate to strong populations. However other areas, especially along the northern Rocky Mountain Front and also the Missouri Breaks, mule deer populations are much lower and have struggled to recover from multi-year droughts coupled with consecutive severe winters in 2022 and 2023. As a result, opportunities to hunt antlerless mule deer are extremely limited across much of Region 4, especially on public land.

A few areas, especially in the southern and central parts of the region have stronger populations and should offer good hunting. Hunters should also note that a few hunting districts in the region have shorter seasons for those holding a general license, while other districts are only open to those who have already drawn a limited entry permit for the district. With several changes enacted this year, hunters should carefully review the regulations for the districts where they intend to hunt.

Hunting access opportunities for mule deer are generally similar to access for white-tailed deer, although some landowners are more restrictive regarding mule deer hunting on their property.

White-tailed Deer

Whitetail populations remain strong across most of Region 4. Although in a few localized areas, outbreaks of epizootic hemorrhagic disease (EHD) in late summer of 2025 had moderate to severe impacts on whitetail populations, and deer numbers in those areas have not yet recovered. As of late summer 2026, EHD has not been reported anywhere in Region 4.

Access to whitetails is generally good across much of the region, although traditionally whitetails are found in greatest numbers in agricultural areas where access is often via private land. All hunters may purchase a single-region antlerless whitetail license, which is valid anywhere in the region except HD 455. Hunters should check for additional whitetail B licenses that may be available surplus after drawings. Hunters willing to harvest antlerless deer may find more landowners willing to grant them permission to hunt private property.

Pronghorn

Primarily due to several years of severe drought conditions, pronghorn populations in western parts of Region 4 entered last winter in less-than-ideal body condition, which led to poor fawn production in the spring of 2026 and low fawn numbers at the present time. As a result of data gathered during aerial surveys conducted in July, biologists have raised pronghorn quotas in a few districts in eastern Region 4, while lowering quotas in other hunting districts in western and northwestern parts of the region. Southern areas near White Sulphur Springs have seen some improvement in pronghorn numbers after several years of severe winters although quotas there remain unchanged for this season. The green-up from the abundant spring rains will mean that pronghorn can be expected to be widely disbursed across the landscape this fall, but as is typically the case, hunters who put in some effort can expect to enjoy high success rates.

Access for pronghorn is generally good across much of the region on public lands, private lands enrolled in the Block Management Program and on other private lands as well.

New York City transit worker killed on the subway tracks
Alan Whyte, Daniel de Vries
6 September 2026

Moet McCullum [Photo: Monet M]

A New York City transit worker was killed by a train late Thursday night, the latest victim in a series of workplace deaths across the United States. Moet McCullum, 41, a conductor with only 11 months on the job and a mother of three, was setting up flagging protection near River Avenue and East 161st Street in the Bronx when a southbound D train struck her just after 11:30 p.m. She was pronounced dead at Lincoln Hospital at 12:42 a.m. Friday. The operator reported seeing no warning lights before the collision.

McCullum normally worked from a conductor’s cab, making announcements, opening and closing the doors and watching the platform. Conductors can also be assigned as construction flaggers. Before a track crew begins work, flaggers walk onto the tracks to place colored warning lights that tell train operator workers are ahead and require them to slow down or stop. While they establish that protection, their safety depends on the control center and dispatchers telling approaching operators where they are.

An internal report by the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA), the state agency that runs New York City’s subways and buses, said McCullum’s supervisor felt wind and heard a train approaching around a curve. A lookout blew a whistle for the workers to clear. The operator said he had been warned that flaggers were on the track but, seeing no warning lights, proceeded at normal speed.

In the center of world finance, subway workers still enter active tracks with hand-placed lamps, whistles and radios. Wall Street’s 2025 bonus pool was $49.2 billion. The MTA’s $21.3 billion 2026 operating budget will send roughly $2.9 billion—13.5 percent of its revenues—to principal and interest on debt. The share is projected to reach 15.8 percent by 2029 as the authority takes on another $18 billion in operating-budget-backed debt.

McCullum’s brother-in-law told the New York Daily News, “We just want justice and the truth. ... There’s just no way a person can go to work and just [get] killed at work.” Her twin sister, also an MTA conductor, wrote on Facebook, “I’m sooo hurt, angry and confused. My heart is literally shattered into pieces.” The collision also undoubtedly traumatized the D train crew.
A subway approaches an above ground station in the Brooklyn borough of New York with the New York City skyline in the background, June 21, 2017. [AP Photo/Bebeto Matthews]

The Democratic Party, which controls New York’s state and city governments, is responsible for enforcing this massive inequality. Governor Kathy Hochul, whose appointees control the MTA, called Transit Workers Union Local 100 President John Chiarello to offer condolences but announced no action on safety.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani has made no public statement on McCullum’s death as of this writing. Mamdani, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, won office by appealing to widespread anger over inequality, exploitation and the cost of living. Since taking office, he has courted Wall Street executives and met twice with President Donald Trump, retained Jessica Tisch—an heir to the billionaire Tisch family—as police commissioner, fired Haitian city employees after the Trump administration stripped them of work authorization, and has sued to block $10,000 bonuses for public school paraprofessionals, among the city’s lowest-paid education workers.

The death on the subway is part of an ongoing industrial slaughterhouse in America. Within roughly 40 hours spanning September 2 and 3, at least five workers were reported killed on the job: Bradley Clouse died in a machine incident at a Kentucky auto parts plant; Ramiro Aaron Sanchez died while maintaining machinery in El Paso; Army Corps employee Robert Scott Pannell was killed beneath a falling tree in Mississippi; and sanitation worker Carl Williams III died beneath an overturned garbage truck in Texas.

On Sunday, at least five were killed and five injured when an Amazon cargo plane overshot the runway and crashed into traffic in Miami.

The Labor Department counted 5,070 fatal workplace injuries in 2024. The AFL-CIO estimates that occupational diseases kill another 135,000 workers each year.

Nearly 240 New York City transit workers have been killed in accidents on the job since 1946, most of them struck by trains. During the pandemic, more than 170 transit workers died from COVID-19.

In November 2023, Hilarion Joseph, 57, also in his first year on the job, was killed by a northbound D train at 34th Street–Herald Square while flagging for a track-cleaning crew. In June 2024, another flagger was critically injured by a train near the Hoyt–Schermerhorn Streets station in Brooklyn.

In 2024, the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) found a growing pattern of safety incidents that created a “substantial risk of death or personal injury.” It recorded 38 near misses involving track workers in 2023, up 58 percent from 2022 and 65 percent from 2021. Its investigators found improper flagging and communications, inadequate track protection, lack of supervision, failures in territory using computerized train control and train-operator inattention.

Failures in flagging and communication have already led to the death of construction flagger Louis Gray Jr. on November 3, 2016 and serious injuries for Jeffrey Fleming. The two men were placing yellow lights on a Brooklyn curve, and the G train operator had not been told they were ahead.

National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) investigators blamed the Rail Control Center’s failure to inform dispatchers that flaggers were on the track. They also cited the MTA’s failure to assess the risks and its decision to permit trains into unprotected work zones. The NTSB recommended that trains be limited to restricted speed while flagging protection was established.

text:
Well. it's interesting...as noted there are flaws in this thesis... If you read this you'll think better. Then go ask your own questions... The flaw in the thesis, point by point
“Cheaper, safer flying and driving.”
Air over a wing is a Navier–Stokes problem. That is true. It is also already solved every day by computational fluid dynamics, wind tunnels, and turbulence models (RANS, LES, wall models). Design bottlenecks are mesh resolution near walls, transition and separation, aeroacoustics, optimization under uncertainty, manufacturing constraints, and fuel/noise regulations. Knowing that a pathological forced solution can blow up does not reduce induced drag on a 737. If anything, a blowup result says: in some extreme regimes the PDE itself is not a trustworthy continuum description. That is a warning label, not a better airfoil.
“Weather you can actually plan around.”
Forecast skill is limited by chaos, incomplete observations, ocean–atmosphere coupling, and unresolved processes (clouds, convection, boundary layers). Those are parameterized because no computer can DNS the atmosphere. Hurricane-track error is not “we lack a theorem that solutions stay in H∞H^\inftyH∞.” Sharper turbulence physics would help; a single existence/blowup theorem is not a turbulence theory. Kolmogorov’s cascade, intermittency, and subgrid models live in a different part of the subject.
“Hearts, stents, and artificial valves.”
Blood is only approximately a Newtonian fluid. The hard parts are non-Newtonian rheology, pulsatile forcing, compliant walls, plaque geometry from imaging, thrombosis, and fluid–structure interaction. Hospitals already run patient-specific CFD from CT/MRI. A Millennium regularity theorem does not design a better leaflet. Better imaging, better constitutive laws, and validated FSI codes do.
“Cleaner power from wind and turbines.”
Same story: blade-resolved LES, wake interactions, stall, compressibility in steam turbines, combustion chemistry in engines. Mixing and heat release are often the limiter, not the abstract smoothness of incompressible NS.
“Ships, pipes, and dirty air.”
Pipe flow is one of the best-studied NS problems on Earth (Moody chart, transition at Re ≈2000\approx 2000≈2000–400040004000). Pollution dispersion is advection–diffusion plus chemistry plus meteorology. Hull slamming is free-surface / multiphase. Those extra physics dominate the Clay idealization (whole-space or periodic, constant viscosity, single-phase, incompressible).
“Buildings, sports, rain.”
Dimples on a golf ball work because they trip the boundary layer; that was understood experimentally long before anyone formalized blowup. Raindrop formation is nucleation, coalescence, and cloud microphysics more than 3D NS regularity.
The last paragraph of the pasted text is the most honest sentence in it: nothing useful happens because a math problem was marked solved. Then it immediately overreaches again: “everything that does happen is going to help engineer a better life.” A correct blowup proof helps engineers only indirectly, and only if people extract mechanisms, regularity criteria, or better models from it.
A more accurate hypothesis
What is actually important about Navier–Stokes
The equations matter because they are the standard continuum expression of momentum conservation for a huge class of materials. That is why they appear in wings, blood, weather, pipes, and stars. Their practical power comes from:
conservation structure (mass, momentum, sometimes energy)
a viscosity that is measurable
a century of special solutions, boundary-layer theory, and numerical methods
You do not need global regularity to use them, any more than you need a completed theory of quantum gravity to use Newtonian gravity for a bridge.
What the Millennium problem is actually about
It is about whether the continuum theory is mathematically closed. Three live interpretations if blowup is real:
The PDE is incomplete. At extreme strain rates you need kinetic theory, molecular effects, compressibility, temperature dependence of viscosity, or some other regularization. Historically, singularities in simplified fluid models have often pointed to missing physics.

Smooth solutions can fail, but only on a set of initial data so thin that every physically relevant flow stays smooth. Then the theorem is deep analysis and almost inert for design.
Blowup is a mathematical shadow of real small-scale intensification (vortex stretching, intermittency). Then the construction might teach us how energy piles up at small scales, which could inform regularity criteria and numerical sensors for “this simulation is about to lie to you.”
That third path is the honest broadening of the hypothesis. The prize problem is a lighthouse for the structure of turbulence, not a substitute for a turbulence model.

What would actually cheapen flight, sharpen forecasts, and improve valves
Higher-quality, cheaper CFD: better discretizations, adaptive meshes, GPU/exascale solvers, differentiable CFD for design
Turbulence closures that are constrained by math and data, not a yes/no smoothness theorem

Experiments and high-Re DNS that measure the things models get wrong
Coupling: structure, heat, chemistry, particles, free surfaces
For weather: observations, data assimilation, and stochastic/ensemble treatment of chaos

For medicine: imaging + non-Newtonian + FSI validation against outcomes, not just prettier velocity fields
A Lean-checked blowup, if it holds, is still a landmark because it tells us the 19th-century continuum model is not a complete existence theory in 3D. That is scientifically important. It is not why your next flight gets cheaper.

The broadened claim, stated carefully
Fluid motion in everyday life is governed, to an excellent approximation, by Navier–Stokes-type balance laws. Engineers already integrate those laws numerically. The Clay problem asks a sharper question: whether that continuum description can remain smooth, or must eventually hand the problem back to physics at smaller scales.
If the new proof is correct, the answer is: the equations can break, at least under a smooth force, while keeping finite energy. That is a result about the model’s consistency, not a new control law for wings, storms, or blood.
The useful sequel is not “we solved fluids.” It is:
extract the blowup mechanism (vortex stretching / self-similar collapse / cancellation between pressure, inertia, and viscosity)
turn that into a priori tests: which norms, if they stay bounded, still guarantee the simulation is meaningful

decide whether real fluids need a corrected continuum theory in those regimes
keep improving the unglamorous stack that actually moves drag, forecast error, and implant performance
That last stack was already the point of fluid dynamics before anyone offered a million dollars for a theorem, and it remains the point after.

text:
Growing up, we romanticize the arrival of freedom. We imagine adulthood as an open door where nobody tells us when to wake up, where to go, or how to live. You reach a certain age and suddenly the world declares you autonomous. But the moment the door swings open, a quiet truth settles in that nobody quite prepared you for: freedom is not the absence of boundaries, but the presence of absolute responsibility.

We convince ourselves we are free to do whatever we desire, but the reality of choice is heavy. Autonomy without accountability is merely drift, and genuine agency requires carrying the weight of your own existence every single day.

"Freedom is not the absence of weight; it is the courage to choose what you carry."

The illusion begins when we mistake being untethered for being liberated. When you are truly free, every consequence points back to you. The path isn’t paved, the safety nets are gone, and the outcome of your life stops being somebody else’s fault. That sudden realization can be deeply overwhelming. There are seasons where the sheer volume of everyday demands leaves you hollowed out, frustrated, and wondering why independence feels less like a triumph and more like exhaustion.

"True adulthood arrives the moment you realize nobody is coming to fix the things you leave broken."

In those moments, the horizon rarely looks promising. Life, in its purest nature, refuses to follow your blueprint. You lay out timelines, design strategies, and invest emotional capital, only to watch circumstances shatter the script without warning. The sheer unpredictability of reality can push anyone to the edge of retreat. We confuse exhaustion with defeat, mistaking a natural desire for rest as an urge to abandon the journey entirely.

"Feeling like giving up is rarely a sign that you are on the wrong path; often, it is simply proof that the terrain has demanded everything you have."

When everything feels chaotic, your mind naturally scans for an exit. It becomes remarkably easy to find reasons to fold, to point at the economy, the background, the timing, or the sheer unfairness of the odds stacked against you. Every obstacle offers a ready-made excuse to walk away, and no one would even blame you for taking it.

"The world will always provide a valid reason to quit, but your life is defined by the one reason you stay."

Beating the odds is not about pretending the struggle does not hurt, nor is it about blind optimism. It is about confronting the messy, unpromising unpredictability of existence and choosing to honor your commitments anyway. You do your absolute best not because an outcome is guaranteed, but because the alternative is surrendering the very autonomy you fought to possess.

"Freedom is not free. It is a daily, relentless responsibility."

To be free is to accept that you are the author, the laborer, and the steward of your own life. It asks you to show up when you are tired, to rebuild when the plan fails, and to refuse the comfortable shelter of an excuse. That weight is not a punishment it is the exact price of an authentic life.

text:
The Deal He Called “Fantastic.” The Ally He Now Treats as a Threat.

In 2018 Donald Trump signed what he called one of the most important and largest trade deals in U.S. and world history. He said the United States, Mexico and Canada “worked so well together.” He said the “terrible NAFTA” would be gone and the USMCA would be “fantastic for all.” He took all the credit. That was his deal.

Then he came back in his 2ne term, called the deal unfair and said who ever did it was stupid (it was him). He spent a year and a half threatening to economically crush Canada, floating annexation as the 51st state, calling our prime minister “Governor,” and treating a neighbour and NATO ally as if it were the problem. Today he directed the GSA to start stripping Canadian-origin products from major U.S. government purchasing schedules unless Canada accepts his version of “reciprocity.” That is the same week Canada’s dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs took effect after talks collapsed.

Look at the actual dairy and agricultural numbers instead of the talking points. Both countries use tariff-rate quotas. Over-quota rates on dairy, poultry, eggs and similar products sit in the same high range on both sides of the border often 200–300%. Canada’s listed over-quota rates are never triggered; those extreme rates have been imposed zero times since 2000 because the quotas exist. The United States runs a comparable system that is never mentioned. Citing the headline percentage while ignoring the quota is how you turn a managed market into a morality play.

The list of reported U.S. demands that helped sink the latest talks goes far beyond dairy: it was an outrageous and insulting offer, a functional veto over major Canadian infrastructure and foreign investment, alignment of Canadian sanctions and export controls with Washington, first-refusal rights and price caps on northern critical minerals, repeal of digital and cultural rules, dismantling of supply management, rewritten auto rules that shift work south, energy allocation priorities, and more. Canada rejected those as incompatible with sovereignty. That is not “ripping off” a partner. That is a country declining to become a supplier on demand.

Canada sent tens of thousands of troops to Afghanistan after 9/11. One hundred and fifty-eight Canadians were killed. When the president later suggested NATO allies “stayed a little back, a little off the front lines,” that is UNTRUE. Canadian veterans who were shot, who buried friends, and who served in Kandahar called it what it was. Recent official mockery of Canadian cadets fits the same pattern. A country that bled beside you is not a joke.

U.S. financing and interference in Canadian fringe movements. Trump's administration have slobbered over Alberta’s resources and tried to use influencers, the administration and a digital army to try and breathe life into “separation” while making it appear there is more support for it then there actually is. During Canada’s last federal campaign he posted that the solution was for Canada to become a state. After the vote, the White House said the election did not change that plan.

The AI videos and images kicking over a Lake Ontario sign and replacing it with “Lake America,” cartoon armies with guns, hockey-stick theatrics of assaulting the prime minister are not statecraft. They are petty. They arrived after Canada asked for seriousness instead of memes. Jealousy of a prime minister who is treated as a serious actor on the world stage and whom is well liked and respected.

He has said Canada is among the toughest countries to deal with tougher than China or Vietnam in his telling and treated the closest ally with a tariff campaign that Canadians now rank America as a greater immediate threat to sovereignty then Russia or China. Projection is the method: accuse Canada of closed markets and bad faith while he is the one who is the bad faith actor.

text:
From 0‑5 to 7‑5: Zheng Qinwen, a Resilience Textbook for China’s Gen‑Z
从0-5到7-5：郑钦文，中国Z世代的“逆商”教科书

September 2026, Arthur Ashe Stadium at Flushing Meadows, New York. Twice in successive rounds, 23‑year‑old Chinese player Zheng Qinwen pulled off a miraculous comeback, winning seven straight games from a crushing 0‑5 deficit. Clawing her way back from World No. 121, she wrote the most electrifying story of this autumn with her racket. And audiences back home — Gen‑Z young people caught in the tug‑of‑war between hustle culture and lying‑flat mindset — found themselves deeply moved.

## Two “0‑5‑to‑7‑5” Comebacks, Nationwide Viral Sensation

Let’s walk through the matches.

In the early hours of September 6 (Beijing Time), during the US Open women’s singles third round, Zheng faced former Australian Open champion Madison Keys. She dropped the opening set 1‑6, and trailed 0‑5 in the decider, with her opponent holding match point. Even renowned commentator Zhan Jun admitted he switched over to watch Premier League football when the score hit 0‑5. Nearly everyone thought the match was over.

Then the miracle unfolded.

Zheng reeled off seven consecutive games to seal the set 7‑5 and complete the comeback. This marked the first time in the Open‑Era women’s Grand‑Slam history that a player had won seven straight games from 0‑5 down in a deciding set to close out a match. US Open official social‑media accounts posted repeatedly, hailing it as “Comeback of the Year” and declaring Zheng “the miracle itself.”

Even more extraordinary followed. In the early hours of September 8, in the fourth round against six‑time Grand‑Slam champion Iga Świątek, Zheng again fell behind 0‑5 in the opening set. Pre‑match AI gave her only a 12 % win probability, and her head‑to‑head record stood at one win against seven losses. Yet the identical drama repeated: seven games in a row, a 7‑5 first‑set victory, and eventually a 2‑0 sweep, returning her to the US Open quarter‑finals after a two‑year gap.

Back‑to‑back “0‑5‑to‑7‑5” epics. Seven straight wins, starting from qualifying rounds all the way to the quarter‑finals. The US Open put Zheng’s “0‑5 moments” alongside Michael Jordan’s iconic Game 6 and Tiger Woods’ legendary Sunday charge, labelling them “incredible.”

## “I just thought, I can’t get bageled — that would be too embarrassing.”

What truly resonated with Gen‑Z was not merely the scoreboard, but what Zheng said afterwards.

After beating Keys, reporters asked what had gone through her mind at 0‑5. Instead of stock phrases about unyielding faith or iron will, she replied with refreshing frankness: “My very first thought was, I can’t get bageled 6‑0. That would be so humiliating.”

That quote went viral overnight.

It felt so authentic. It echoes the inner monologue many young people face amid looming deadlines: “I have to hand this in; I can’t submit a blank page.” Free from polished elite‑athlete packaging, Zheng voiced the relatable, almost self‑deprecating instinct of ordinary youth — yet paired with superhuman execution.

Equally touching was her reference to lines from *Rainbow Sea*, a Chinese animated series from her childhood: *“Those who believe in miracles are just as extraordinary as miracles themselves.”*

A post‑00s athlete, standing under the bright lights of Arthur Ashe Stadium, quoting lines from a domestic cartoon she grew up watching. This was no deliberate cultural‑export performance; it was natural Gen‑Z cultural memory. It struck a chord with millions who remembered weekday evenings glued to TV screens, stirred by those passionate lines. Competitive spirit merged seamlessly with a generation’s childhood nostalgia.

Jay Chou shared her interview clip late at night with the comment “What a comeback,” while Hannah Quin‑livan echoed “the spirit of never giving up.” The story exploded beyond sports circles. Hashtags about Zheng’s historic comebacks topped social‑media trending lists.

## From World No. 121 to Seven‑Match Win Streak: A Narrative of Rock‑Bottom Rebuilding

Zheng’s story resonates so deeply with Gen‑Z because it mirrors many young people’s own life journeys.

At the 2024 Paris Olympics, she claimed China’s first‑ever women’s singles tennis gold, soaring to World No. 4. That was her shining peak, comparable to landing a dream offer, getting into graduate school or launching a successful project — brimming with optimism for what lay ahead.

Then reality delivered a heavy blow. Elbow surgery kept her sidelined for almost 10 months. After returning, she suffered at least six first‑round exits. Her 2026 tour record stood at 11 wins versus 13 losses, a win‑rate below 50 %, her worst run in five years. Her ranking plummeted from No. 4 all the way down to No. 121.

Falling from stardom to rock‑bottom, from nationwide high‑expectation to public doubts whether “she had lost her edge.” Gen‑Z knows this kind of whiplash all too well. Many young adults go through their own “ranking collapse”: failed postgraduate entrance exams, frustrating job‑hunts, workplace plateaus, or the sober realisation that hard work does not always guarantee reward.

But Zheng refused to lie flat. Having to play qualifying matches to reach the main draw was psychologically crushing for a former Olympic champion. She openly acknowledged feeling upset and demoralised upon learning she would start in qualifiers. Yet soon she reframed her mindset: “This is reality, so I might as well approach it positively. Qualifiers have produced Grand‑Slam champions before. I’ll give it everything I’ve got.”

Seven consecutive victories from qualifying into the quarter‑finals, her live ranking rebounding to No. 52. This is not hollow motivational fluff. It is genuine testimony of one person rebuilding herself brick‑by‑brick after total collapse.

## “Queen Wen”: What Kind of Icon Does Gen‑Z Need?

Zheng Qinwen embodies distinctly Gen‑Z qualities.

She is unapologetically confident. After her 2024 Olympic triumph, she stated plainly: “The title ‘Queen Wen’ is well‑deserved.” No false modesty, no awkward hedging, she gracefully embraced praise. That self‑assured sense of “I deserve this” strikes a chord with Gen‑Z, tired of old‑fashioned social pressure urging people not to stand out. Young audiences admire someone who can openly say “I am good.”

She is authentic. She lies flat on‑court overwhelmed by joy after victories; she sheds genuine tears in defeat. She does not sugar‑coat losses with empty phrases like “honourable defeat,” instead honestly admitting “I know I could have played better.” After matches, she stays on‑court practising serves when dissatisfied with her first‑serve percentage. That unpretentious authenticity carries far more power than any manufactured perfect public persona.

She carries herself globally. Fluent English, sharp logical thinking, calm and equal‑footed when interviewed by international journalists. She can pinpoint her own technical weaknesses, yet accept losses philosophically with “that is tennis.” As she once observed: “The younger generation views the world with equal respect. This mirrors China’s progress. Only by meeting the world eye‑to‑eye can we fully bring out our authentic, stronger selves.”

She does not stoke anxiety, nor peddle simplistic narratives that “hard work always guarantees success.” Instead, she presents a far more realistic blueprint for growth: falling low, feeling dejected, doubting yourself — yet choosing to stand back up, point‑by‑point, game‑by‑game.

Is this not exactly the story our generation needs to hear?

Why has Zheng Qinwen become a spiritual touchstone for Gen‑Z?

Not merely for winning matches, but for refusing to surrender while trailing 0‑5. Not merely for winning Olympic gold, but for refusing to give up when her ranking sank to 121. Not for being flawless, but for openly showing us **what it looks like to rebuild your life from the ruins**.

*“Those who believe in miracles are just as extraordinary as miracles themselves.”*

These words go to Zheng Qinwen — and to every one of us slogging through our personal “0‑5” moments, fighting point by point to turn things around.

    2026年9月，纽约法拉盛公园的阿瑟·阿什球场，郑钦文连续两轮在0-5落后的绝境中连赢七局完成逆转。一个从世界第121位爬回来的23岁中国姑娘，用球拍写下了这个秋天最燃的剧本。而屏幕这头的我们——一群在"内卷"和"躺平"之间反复横跳的Z世代——突然被击中了。

【两场"让五追七"，一次全网沸腾】
    先说比赛。
    北京时间9月6日凌晨，美网女单第三轮，郑钦文对阵前澳网冠军凯斯。首盘1-6速败，决胜盘0-5落后，对手手握赛点。解说员詹俊坦言"看到0-5就转台看英超了"，几乎所有人都以为故事结束了。
    然后，奇迹发生了。
    郑钦文连赢七局，以7-5完成逆转。这是公开赛年代女子大满贯历史上首次出现决胜盘0-5落后连赢七局终结比赛的情况。美网官方连发推文，称其为"年度最佳逆转"，直言郑钦文"就是奇迹本身"。
    更炸裂的还在后面。9月8日凌晨，第四轮对阵六届大满贯冠军斯瓦泰克，郑钦文首盘再次0-5落后。赛前AI预测她的胜率仅为12%，两人历史交手1胜7负。但同样的剧本再次上演——连追七局，7-5拿下首盘，最终2-0横扫对手，时隔两年重返美网八强。
    连续两轮"让五追七"，从资格赛一路七连胜杀进八强。美网官方将郑钦文的"0-5时刻"与乔丹的神奇第6场、老虎伍兹的神奇周日并列，评价为"不可思议"。

【"总不能让她打个6-0吧，太丢人了"】
    但真正让Z世代集体破防的，不是比分本身，而是郑钦文说的那些话。
    逆转凯斯后，记者问她0-5落后时在想什么。她没有搬出"永不放弃""信念坚定"之类的标准答案，而是特别不好意思地说："当时脑子里第一个想法就是，总不能让她打个6-0吧，那也太丢人了。"
    这句话瞬间刷屏。
    太真实了。这不就是我们面对deadline时的心理活动吗？"反正都要交，总不能交个空白的吧。"郑钦文用一种去精英化的、带着自嘲的真实感，拉近了和年轻观众的距离。她不是那种被包装出来的"完美运动员"，她就是一个会在绝境中因为"丢人"二字激发斗志的普通年轻人——只不过这个普通人的执行力，强到逆天。
    更让人共鸣的是赛后她引用的那句台词，来自童年动画片《星游记》："相信奇迹的人本身就和奇迹一样了不起。"
    一个00后运动员，在法拉盛公园的聚光灯下，引用自己小时候看过的国产动画台词。这不是刻意的文化输出，而是一种自然的、属于Z世代的文化记忆。它击中了无数人的童年——那些放学后守在电视机前的傍晚，那些被一句台词点燃的中二热血。竞技精神与一代人的文化记忆，在这一刻无缝连接。
周杰伦深夜转发郑钦文采访截图并配文"这个逆转"，昆凌同步感叹"不放弃的精神"，话题从体育圈炸向大众圈层。"郑钦文美网惊天逆转""郑钦文决胜盘连赢7局"等话题登顶热搜。

【从第121位到七连胜：一场关于"触底反弹"的叙事】
    郑钦文的故事之所以让Z世代如此共情，还因为它太像我们自己的经历了。
    2024年巴黎奥运会，她拿下中国首枚网球女单金牌，世界排名飙升至第四。那是她的高光时刻，像极了我们拿到offer、考上研、项目上线的那些瞬间——意气风发，觉得未来一片光明。
    然后，现实给了她一记重拳。右肘手术，休战近10个月。复出后遭遇至少6次"一轮游"，2026赛季巡回赛战绩11胜13负，胜率不足50%，创近五年新低。世界排名从第4位一路跌至第121位。
    从云端跌到谷底，从被万众期待到被质疑"是不是不行了"。这种落差感，Z世代太熟悉了。我们中的很多人，正在经历类似的"排名暴跌"——可能是考研失利、求职碰壁、职场瓶颈，或者仅仅是发现"努力不一定有回报"这个残酷真相。
    但郑钦文没有躺平。她需要打资格赛才能进入美网正赛，这对一个曾经的奥运冠军来说，心理落差可想而知。她坦言得知要打资格赛时"一时难以接受，甚至有些消沉"，但几天后她想通了："反正都要面对，不如用更加积极一点的态度。资格赛选手也有在美网夺冠的先例，放手一搏吧。"
    从资格赛一路杀进八强，七连胜。即时世界排名回升至第52位。这不是鸡汤，这是一个人在废墟里一砖一瓦重建自己的真实记录。

【"Queen Wen"：Z世代需要什么样的偶像】
    郑钦文身上有一种气质，特别"Z世代"。
    她自信。2024年巴黎奥运会夺冠后，她说"'Queen Wen'这个词，我实至名归。"没有谦虚，没有扭捏，坦坦荡荡地接受赞美。这种"我值得"的底气，是Z世代最欣赏的品质——我们厌倦了"枪打出头鸟"的规训，渴望看到一个人大大方方地说"我就是很强"。
    她真实。赢球了会激动到躺倒在场地中央，输球了会哽咽落泪。她不会用"虽败犹荣"来粉饰失利，而是直接说"我觉得我应该打得更好"。她会在赛后拉着教练加练发球，因为对一发进球率不满意。这种"不装"的态度，比任何完美人设都更有感染力。
    她国际化。流利的英语，清晰的逻辑，面对全球媒体时不卑不亢。她能具体分析自己的技术短板，也能在失利时保持"这就是网球"的豁达。正如她曾说过的："年轻一代平视世界，同时代表了中国的进步，只有平视这个世界，才能把真正的、完整的自己更强地发挥出来。"
    她不贩卖焦虑，也不鼓吹"努力就能成功"的简单叙事。她展示的是一个更真实的成长模型：会跌倒，会消沉，会怀疑自己，但每一次都选择站起来，一分一分地往回追。
    这不就是我们这代人最需要听到的故事吗？

    回到最终的问题：为什么郑钦文能成为Z世代的精神图腾？
    不是因为她赢了比赛，而是因为她在0-5落后时没有放弃；不是因为她拿了金牌，而是因为她在排名跌至121位时没有躺平；不是因为她完美无缺，而是因为她真实地展示了"一个人如何在废墟中重建自己"的全过程。
    "相信奇迹的人本身就和奇迹一样了不起。"
    这句话，送给郑钦文，也送给每一个正在"0-5落后"的人生阶段里，咬牙一分一分往回追的你和我。

text:
Former acting CIA Director Michael Morell says the agency knew al Qaeda wanted to strike the United States before 9/11. What it didn’t know was when, where or how.

Twenty-five years after the attacks, Morell tells the Mo News podcast that missing tactical intelligence—not a failure to recognize the broader threat—left the U.S. unable to stop the plot that ultimately killed nearly 3,000 Americans.

Morell, who served as President George W. Bush’s intelligence briefer and was with him in Florida on 9/11, defended the now-famous August 6, 2001, Presidential Daily Brief titled “Bin Ladin Determined To Strike in US.” He said the document warned of al Qaeda’s intent to attack but offered no indication that a specific plot was imminent.

Speaking to Mo News last week, Morell drew a distinction between strategic warning—knowing an enemy has the intent and ability to strike—and tactical warning, which requires penetrating a plot to learn its timing, location and method.

“We didn’t have that prior to 9/11,” Morell said. “We had it in spades after 9/11.”

He partly attributed the intelligence gap to shrinking resources during the 1990s, when the CIA’s budget and workforce each declined by roughly 25%.

Ultimately, Morell said, “bin Laden got lucky,” launching the plot during the transition from the Clinton administration to the Bush administration.

text:
Tonight, the Manvel City Council voted to end our relationship with Flock Safety.

As part of that direction, staff has been instructed to immediately cover the Flock cameras operating in Manvel and send the required 30-day notice to terminate our agreement. If Flock has not removed its cameras within those 30 days, the City will remove them.

I want to be clear about something I have said throughout this discussion: I support our Police Department, I support our officers, and I support the responsible use of technology to keep Manvel safe.

My concern is with Flock Safety and the direction this technology and company are heading.

And over the last few weeks, those concerns have only grown.

In Sheboygan, Wisconsin, city officials learned that their Flock cameras were collecting more than license plates. According to city officials and local reporting, the cameras were also generating information about traffic volume, vehicle types, speeds and movement patterns. The city says it did not know this information was being collected. How did they find out? A Flock representative offered to sell them access to a new feature for their cameras that was built in and working. Sheboygan covered its cameras and moved to terminate its contract. 

Here in Texas, Pflugerville recently terminated its Flock agreement after discovering that more than 400 outside agencies had accessed its system when the city says only 83 partner agencies were authorized. Records subsequently reported that 459 outside agencies conducted approximately 1.6 million searches of Pflugerville’s camera network over a six-month period. 

At the same time, Flock’s technology is rapidly expanding beyond simply reading license plates. Its newer AI-powered investigative tools can combine camera information with other databases and allow officers to conduct broad searches based on vehicle descriptions, movements, relationships and other information. 

Technology is moving incredibly fast. Government has a responsibility to make sure accountability, transparency and constitutional protections don’t get left behind.

This was never about being anti-police or anti-technology. It’s about asking a simple question:

How much surveillance are we willing to accept in the name of safety, and who ultimately controls the information being collected about our citizens?

I believe we can provide our officers with effective technology without building or participating in a nationwide surveillance network controlled by a private, for-profit company.

Tonight, Council made the decision to move Manvel in a different direction.

Safety and liberty do not have to be mutually exclusive. We can protect both.

The Scorpion and the Frog

A scorpion approached a frog who waited at the riverbank.
“Carry me across,” the scorpion said, “for I cannot swim.”

The frog eyed him with weary caution.
“You are a creature of the sting. If I take you upon my back, you will strike me. We will both drown.”

The scorpion replied with smooth logic.
“If I sting you in the water, I perish as well. It would be against nature and reason.”

The frog, persuaded by this argument, allowed the scorpion to climb aboard. He swam out, strong legs pushing through the current.

Halfway across, the sharp agony of a sting pierced his back. His muscles faltered. As both began to sink beneath the river’s surface, the frog gasped:

“You promised! Why would you do this?”

The scorpion’s voice held neither anger nor triumph, only a resigned truth.
“Silly frog! You knew I was a scorpion when you offered to ferry me across the river.”

They vanished into the cold deep together.

text:
Tocqueville argued that free societies depend on strong institutions between individuals and centralized power. Atomization erodes both the habits and the organized capacity for self-government. As those institutions weaken, centralized power grows.

In Democracy in America, associations are not just barriers against the state. For Tocqueville, free association is a school of self-government, where people learn to cooperate, organize, deliberate, lead, and act together.

He asks:
“How can a populace, unaccustomed to freedom in small concerns, learn to use it temperately in great affairs?”

And on the danger of atomization:
“What resistance can be offered to tyranny in a country where every private individual is impotent, and where the citizens are united by no common tie?”

More sharply:
“Despotism... is never more secure of continuance than when it can keep men asunder.”

For Tocqueville then, freedom requires more than rights. It requires institutions where people practice self-government. Families, churches, towns, and free associations build the habits and organized capacity for common action.

Without them, people may remain formally free while becoming socially atomized, politically passive, and practically dependent on centralized power. Liberty survives on paper while the capacity for self-government withers.

Experiences with Maha Periyava: Spend this money on temples and care of cows. Serve milk and bread to the poor. All these are very great acts of merit.”

Periyaval was circumambulating the Kamakshiamman temple through the quadrangular streets having started from Kolla Chatram, which is situated in the southern side. It was raining heavily. He had draped a gunny sack on His head and shoulders. He did not have even a bamboo umbrella. Four of us accompanied Him. Vedapuri, Srikantan, Bank Ramamurthi and I. When Periyava was walking on the road running along the northern wall of the temple, a big car came up the road and slowed down. A north Indian got down and asked in Hindi, “Where is Shankaracharya Maharaj?”

“That person walking in the front with a sack upon His head, that is Shankaracharya…”

The gentleman was stunned. He gazed with wonder at Periyava who was walking on the road, getting drenched in rain. “Why does not Swamiji go by car?”

“Periyava does not get into a car.”

The gentleman’s eyes filled with tears. Periyava turned and looked. He asked the attendants what it was all about and apprising Himself on the matter, sent word that the gentleman go by car to Kolla Chatram and wait there for Him. The gentleman left. After the darsan of Kamakshi, Periyava returned to Kolla Chatram. The gentleman from the North prostrated with great reverence and attempted to place a large amount of money in front of Periyaval as an offering.

“Why do I need money? You have a good heart. Spend this money on temples and care of cows. Serve milk and bread to the poor. All these are very great acts of merit.”

The wealthy gentleman did not expect this reply. “I have seen several ascetics, pontiffs and religious leaders and have also offered large sums of money. Gauging that I am a rich man they would invariably say, ‘I do many charitable deeds. What you have offered is a small sum. You must make a bigger offering.’ I expected the same here. But Periyava is not impressed with money at all. It is rare to see such a Swamiji.”

The gentleman spoke several words in praise of Periyava. Periyava reciprocated the gesture and said, “You have a generous nature, an exemplary nature. You have the good heart to spend your wealth in acts of charity.”
On this occasion, Periyava rejected several thousands of rupees. On another occasion He did not accept some crores of rupees offered by an industrialist. Who is to know His heart?

He didn’t exactly "demolish" it in the way of destroying a church in anger. It was a state project to build the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus.

The site: That spot in Damascus had been a place of worship for over 1000 years.
- Aramean temple to Hadad → 
- Roman temple to Jupiter → 
- Church of St. John the Baptist built by Christians in the 4th century CE → 
- Early mosque + church side by side after Muslims took Damascus peacefully in 634 CE

After 634, Muslims and Christians made an agreement. The church stayed with Christians, and Muslims prayed in a part of the courtyard. Both shared the site for ∼70 years.

 Al-Walid replaced it in 705, because Al-Walid wanted to make Damascus the capital of a huge Islamic empire and give it a grand congregational mosque. Reasons historians give:

Political + religious statement: The Umayyads wanted a monument that showed Damascus as the center of the Muslim world, like the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem.

Not enough space: The Muslim community had grown huge. Praying in a small section of the courtyard wasn’t enough for Friday prayers.

Compensation: According to Muslim and Christian sources like Ibn Asakir, Al-Walid negotiated with the Christians. He offered to buy the church and build them new churches elsewhere in Damascus with state money. Most Christians agreed. Some sources say a small group refused at first.

The relic: The church housed what was believed to be the head of John the Baptist/Yahya عليه السلام. When they built the mosque, that shrine was kept and incorporated inside the mosque. It’s still there today.

So it wasn’t razed and left empty. The church structure was dismantled and the Great Umayyad Mosque was built on the same site 705-715 CE.

It was not forced. There's are many cases today in America where Muslims are buying churches
