text:
$AMKR AMKOR’S $12 BILLION ARIZONA EXPANSION: STRATEGIC VALIDATION AND A LARGER CAPITAL-RETURN TEST

INVESTMENT ASSESSMENT

Amkor’s September 2026 Arizona expansion strengthens the evidence that domestic advanced packaging is becoming a durable customer requirement rather than a largely policy-driven manufacturing initiative. The financial interpretation is more conditional. Planned campus investment increases to approximately $12 billion from an existing $7 billion, 2-phase development plan, making the incremental capital commitment approximately $5 billion, or 71.4 percent. The announcement therefore represents a substantial enlargement of an established project, not an entirely new $12 billion investment. Customer commitments exceeding phase 1 capacity improve demand visibility, but the release does not establish phase 2 utilization guarantees, contracted profitability, or an attractive return on the enlarged capital base. Amkor Technology

The central investment distinction is between strategic relevance and economic value capture. Amkor is becoming more deeply embedded in the U.S. semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem through customer-backed capacity expansion and technology collaboration. That positioning can support longer program duration, greater packaging content, and improved customer retention. However, shareholders benefit only if these advantages produce sufficient pricing, utilization, and cash generation to compensate for construction expenditure, equipment depreciation, qualification costs, and financing requirements. The expansion reduces uncertainty about customer interest while increasing the importance of execution and capital discipline.

The announcement is consequently more consequential for the durability and scale of earnings beyond the initial Arizona ramp than for near-term earnings. A constructive interpretation rests on customers increasingly sharing the investment burden and committing to capacity before it becomes available. A cautious interpretation rests on Amkor undertaking a larger investment cycle before demonstrating the operating economics of its initial U.S. production capacity. These interpretations are not mutually exclusive.

WHAT HAS CHANGED, AND WHAT HAS NOT

Phase 2 is expected to add 60,000 square meters of cleanroom space to phase 1’s 33,000 square meters, bringing the campus to approximately 93,000 square meters. Construction is anticipated to begin in late 2027 and finish by the end of 2029. No explicit phase 2 production-start date accompanies that construction schedule. Earlier disclosures placed phase 1 construction completion in 2027 and production commencement in early 2028. Building completion, equipment installation, customer qualification, production commencement, and mature utilization must therefore remain separate milestones in financial projections. Amkor Technology

The cleanroom comparison requires consistent denominators. The enlarged campus is approximately 2.82 times the size of phase 1, but the October 2025 plan already included a subsequent facility and more than 750,000 square feet of combined cleanroom space. That earlier reference converts to approximately 69,700 square meters. Relative to that reference, the newly announced footprint is approximately 33.5 percent larger, although the precise increase is lower to the extent the previous plan exceeded 750,000 square feet. Neither a 182 percent increase in space relative to phase 1 nor a 71.4 percent increase in the campus budget should be presented as the increase in economic production capacity. Amkor Technology

The difference between expenditure growth and floor-space growth warrants scrutiny, but does not establish a cost overrun. Greater process intensity, more expensive equipment, expanded test capability, infrastructure requirements, and a different product mix could all increase investment faster than cleanroom area. The relevant reconciliation is the change in buildings, shared infrastructure, equipment, process scope, and production capability against the earlier budget. Importantly, the $5 billion increase is the change in total planned campus expenditure; it is not a disclosed standalone budget for the entirety of phase 2.

The demand signal is also incremental rather than wholly new. Management had already described phase 1 as fully committed on the July 2026 earnings call. September’s announcement extends that signal by stating that commitments have surpassed the planned initial capacity. It does not disclose how much of the additional space is covered, which programs underpin the expansion, or the commercial enforceability of those commitments. The correct inference is stronger evidence supporting expansion beyond phase 1, not proof that the entire enlarged campus is sold out. Amkor Technology

CUSTOMER COMMITMENTS ARE BECOMING MORE SUBSTANTIVE

The customer framework is stronger than a collection of nonbinding expressions of interest. In June 2026, TSMC and Amkor announced a 10-year agreement establishing a framework for TSMC to procure advanced packaging and testing services from Amkor in Arizona. In July, Amkor announced a $1.5 billion, multi-year advanced packaging and development agreement with NVIDIA, including a customer prepayment supporting U.S. capacity expansion. These arrangements provide more tangible evidence of customer alignment than the construction announcement alone. Neither public announcement, however, specifies minimum annual revenue, guaranteed operating returns, or comprehensive cancellation protection. Amkor Technology

The distinction between capacity reservations and economic underwriting is fundamental. A customer can commit to a manufacturing platform while retaining flexibility over program timing, product mix, or actual purchases. Conversely, a contract with enforceable minimum payments, cancellation compensation, and reimbursement of dedicated equipment can materially reduce investment risk even before utilization becomes visible. The relevant underwriting variables are the proportion of fixed costs covered during ramp, the treatment of unused capacity, the duration of pricing protection, and the allocation of technology-transition costs. Contract duration alone does not resolve these questions.

Customer relationships also should not be counted as independent pools of demand without examining the procurement channel. TSMC may procure packaging services for a device ultimately designed or purchased by another announced partner. The same physical production flow could therefore appear in descriptions of the foundry partnership, the end-customer relationship, and the domestic manufacturing initiative. The public agreements establish ecosystem alignment, but not additive revenue streams equal to the sum of each participant’s stated commitment. Modeling should follow actual manufacturing steps, contractual counterparties, and invoiced services. Amkor Technology

Apple provides an important counterweight to interpreting the entire Arizona opportunity as AI infrastructure. Apple has identified itself as the initial and largest customer for the new Amkor facility and has described packaging and testing Apple silicon manufactured at TSMC Arizona. This supports a broader domestic semiconductor manufacturing thesis rather than an exclusively data-center thesis. It also introduces different volume patterns and commercial economics: high-volume mobile programs can help absorb infrastructure costs, but their pricing, seasonality, package requirements, and product cycles need not resemble those of large AI accelerators. Apple

TECHNOLOGY CONTENT MATTERS MORE THAN CLEANROOM AREA

Amkor’s opportunity is not simply to perform more conventional assembly in a different geography. Its advanced packaging platforms address heterogeneous integration, including the combination of logic chiplets and memory through dense interconnect structures. Amkor’s S-SWIFT platform, for example, uses redistribution layers to provide short die-to-die connections and offers an alternative to certain silicon-interposer-based approaches. This creates potential value through package architecture, integration capability, and manufacturability, rather than through labor-intensive assembly alone. Amkor Technology

The economic consequence is that package complexity can increase revenue content even when unit growth is moderate. Larger packages, additional interconnect layers, more demanding die placement, tighter electrical requirements, and expanded testing can require more processing per finished device. However, these same characteristics can increase equipment requirements and reduce throughput. A factory can therefore report rising revenue per package while experiencing weaker capital productivity. Revenue per cleanroom area is insufficient; the more useful measures are gross profit per constrained tool-hour, qualified output per unit of invested capital, and cash generation after equipment replacement.

High-density fan-out also creates both opportunity and technology-selection risk. Amkor’s SWIFT technology supports fine-line routing and high-density interconnects, while its broader heterogeneous packaging work spans silicon-interposer, redistribution-layer, and bridge-based approaches. A flexible platform can address multiple architectures, but different process flows require different tool configurations and qualification work. An investment in general advanced packaging capacity should not automatically be treated as interchangeable capacity for every future AI package architecture. The value of the new footprint depends on how efficiently equipment can be redeployed as customer designs evolve. Amkor Technology

Yield economics deserve particular attention because system value and Amkor’s revenue are not equivalent. Amkor states that customer wafers are generally consigned, with title and risk of loss generally remaining with the customer. The value of the underlying processor therefore should not be counted as Amkor packaging revenue, nor should its full value automatically be assumed to represent Amkor’s financial liability. Nevertheless, qualification failures, manufacturing defects, and contractual quality obligations can still create substantial commercial costs through rework, delayed shipments, customer claims, and lost program allocation. Amkor Technology

An illustrative yield sensitivity demonstrates the operating leverage without assuming an actual Amkor yield. Holding processing cost per production start constant, a reduction in good-unit yield from 95 percent to 90 percent raises processing cost per good unit by approximately 5.6 percent. That increase occurs before any additional rework or customer compensation. A high-value packaging facility can consequently remain commercially attractive while producing disappointing margins during process learning. Customer commitments reduce demand uncertainty, but do not eliminate this manufacturing risk.

THE DOMESTIC ECOSYSTEM ADVANTAGE IS REAL, BUT NOT EXCLUSIVE

Arizona can improve Amkor’s competitive position by placing advanced packaging closer to domestic wafer fabrication and aligning qualification, logistics, and customer support within the same manufacturing ecosystem. The TSMC agreement explicitly supports procurement of Amkor’s packaging and testing services. The potential benefit is not simply shorter transportation distance; it is a more coordinated route from fabricated wafer to tested device, with fewer organizational handoffs and better alignment of capacity expansion. The magnitude of that benefit will depend on the actual division of work between the companies. Amkor Technology

That partnership should not be interpreted as exclusive control over U.S. advanced packaging. TSMC’s published Arizona plans include its own advanced packaging facilities. Intel also opened Fab 9 in New Mexico for high-volume advanced packaging, including Foveros technology, in January 2024. Amkor’s differentiation is its role as an outsourced semiconductor assembly and test provider offering a domestic platform, not the absence of any competing U.S. advanced packaging capability. Different providers may also occupy complementary steps within the same manufacturing flow rather than compete for an identical service bundle. TSMC

The most durable competitive advantage would combine qualified processes, customer-specific design engagement, reliable execution, and economically efficient scale. Geographic location can strengthen that combination, but location alone is unlikely to secure attractive margins indefinitely. Once customers have multiple qualified domestic options, procurement pressure can shift toward price and productivity. The contractual allocation of cost reductions therefore matters: greater automation and yield improvement create more shareholder value when Amkor retains a meaningful portion of the savings.

Domestic packaging also does not, by itself, create a completely domestic supply chain. Packaging remains dependent on wafers, substrates, materials, equipment, and potentially memory components supplied through broader manufacturing networks. Amkor’s annual disclosures identify the importance of externally sourced substrates and other packaging materials. The appropriate strategic conclusion is reduced dependence on particular offshore manufacturing steps, not elimination of international supply-chain exposure. Amkor Technology

THE FUNDING REQUIREMENT IS MATERIAL DESPITE STRONGER CUSTOMER SUPPORT

Amkor entered this larger investment commitment with approximately $2.5 billion of cash and short-term investments, approximately $2.5 billion of debt, and $3.6 billion of total liquidity at June 2026. Reported debt to trailing EBITDA was approximately 1.8 times. This provides meaningful financing flexibility, but the liquidity figure includes the cash balance; it is not an additional $3.6 billion available on top of cash. Similarly, an approximately balanced cash-and-debt position should not be confused with an absence of funding risk during a substantial construction cycle. Amkor Technology

Internal cash generation remains well below planned investment. During 1H 2026, operating cash flow was approximately $382 million against capital expenditure of approximately $688 million. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was therefore approximately negative $307 million. Amkor’s reported free cash flow was approximately negative $270 million because its definition also included roughly $37 million of proceeds from property disposals and grants. The difference is relevant when assessing recurring funding capacity rather than reported cash-flow presentation. Amkor Technology

The existing 2026 capital expenditure outlook of $2.5 billion to $3.0 billion implies approximately $1.81 billion to $2.31 billion of spending in 2H 2026 after deducting the 1H outlay. That represents an average quarterly spending pace approximately 2.6–3.4 times the 1H average. Actual disbursements remain sensitive to construction progress and equipment timing, but the arithmetic demonstrates the near-term cash requirement before phase 2 construction begins. The enlarged campus plan should be assessed against a year-by-year cash bridge, not against aggregate liquidity in isolation. Amkor Technology

The May 2026 issuance of $1.15 billion of 0 percent convertible notes improved financing flexibility without a recurring cash coupon. It nevertheless created a liability maturing in 2031, alongside potential conversion-related equity consequences. The absence of a coupon does not make the financing economically free, and the proceeds are already reflected in the June balance sheet. The maturity also falls close enough to the anticipated phase 2 ramp that refinancing capacity and cash generation during the early 2030s deserve explicit attention. Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP

NVIDIA’S PREPAYMENT IS VALUABLE FINANCING, NOT A PERMANENT SUBSIDY

Management stated that NVIDIA’s $1.5 billion prepayment is expected in 2027 and will be returned through the provision of U.S. services over an anticipated period of approximately 5–10 years. This substantially improves the alignment between customer demand and Amkor’s capital expenditure. However, it is not an equity investment, an immediately recognized revenue contribution, or a grant that permanently reduces the cost of the factory without an offsetting obligation. It advances the timing of cash that is economically associated with future service delivery. Amkor Technology

The benefit is meaningful even under that more conservative interpretation. Prefunding can reduce external financing needs, lower cash-interest exposure, and provide stronger evidence of customer commitment than an unsupported demand forecast. The corresponding cost is reduced future cash collection as services are delivered against the advance. A valuation that adds the prepayment to present liquidity while also assuming full future cash collection on the associated revenue would double count value.

Customer advances also differ in their terms. Amkor disclosed other expected advance payments requiring standby letters of credit, including a $100 million payment received in July 2026. Those arrangements should not automatically be assumed to have the same protections or requirements as the separately announced NVIDIA agreement. Refund provisions, performance milestones, collateral requirements, and the schedule of service credits determine how much practical financing benefit each advance provides. Amkor Technology

TAX-CREDIT ELIGIBILITY IS A CENTRAL RETURN VARIABLE

The current federal advanced manufacturing investment credit is 35 percent for qualifying property placed in service after 2025, rather than the earlier 25 percent rate. This makes the eligible investment base a major determinant of Arizona’s economics. The percentage cannot simply be applied to every dollar in a corporate investment headline: eligibility depends on the property, qualifying basis, taxpayer requirements, and applicable construction rules. The timing of cash realization also remains distinct from the economic value of the credit. IRS

Phase 2’s anticipated late-2027 construction start creates an important technical question because the credit generally excludes property whose construction begins after December 31, 2026. That does not automatically make phase 2 ineligible. Treasury regulations permit multiple qualifying properties or facilities to be treated as a single manufacturing project for construction-start purposes, subject to ownership and specified integration factors. These include contiguous land, shared utilities, common contracts, permits, or financing. A later physical construction phase can therefore potentially rely on an earlier qualifying project start. IRS

The relevant conclusion is conditional rather than binary. Amkor’s phased campus structure provides a plausible route to eligibility, but a press-release construction schedule does not establish the tax result. The determination requires the actual project structure, qualifying work, applicable continuity requirements, and eligible asset base. Neither assuming that all phase 2 expenditure earns the credit nor excluding it solely because construction begins in 2027 is sufficiently supported.

The sensitivity is substantial. Applying a 35 percent credit to the entire $5 billion incremental investment would produce $1.75 billion of credits and leave $3.25 billion of capital to be funded before working capital, financing costs, and timing effects. This is an upper-bound illustration for that credit, not a forecast of qualifying expenditure. Every 10-percentage-point reduction in the proportion of eligible spending would reduce the credit by $175 million. Eligibility uncertainty can therefore have greater valuation significance than modest changes in near-term quarterly earnings.

The existing CHIPS award is separate. The federal government finalized an award of up to $407 million tied to project milestones, and Amkor disclosed that it had not received those funds as of June 2026. The award should not be assumed to increase automatically with the campus budget. Amkor also records qualifying investment credits and grants as reductions to the carrying value of property, plant, and equipment. Consequently, incentives can affect subsequent depreciation and reported margins as well as cash funding; they are not simply benefits flowing through the income-tax line. NIST

THE EXISTING BUSINESS IS IMPROVING, BUT REPORTED EARNINGS REQUIRE NORMALIZATION

Amkor’s underlying operating momentum provides a stronger starting point for this investment cycle than a stagnant legacy business would. Q2 2026 revenue was approximately $1.898 billion, up approximately 26 percent, with a 16.8 percent gross margin, approximately $200 million of operating income, and $0.70 of diluted EPS. Q3 guidance called for $1.95 billion to $2.05 billion of revenue, an 18.5–19.5 percent gross margin, and $0.72–$0.82 of EPS. The improving gross-margin outlook supports the proposition that higher-value packaging can improve the consolidated business mix. Amkor Technology

Reported Q2 profitability nevertheless included a $21 million real-estate sale gain and $14 million of discrete tax benefits. Removing the property gain reduces operating margin to approximately 9.4 percent from 10.5 percent. Removing that gain at an illustrative 20 percent tax rate and deducting the discrete tax benefit produces approximately $0.57 of EPS. This is an analytical normalization, not a company-reported adjusted measure. The implication is not that operating improvement is absent, but that the reported $0.70 should not be treated as an entirely recurring earnings base. Amkor Technology

The portfolio also remains broader than AI packaging. Communications represented 42 percent of Q2 sales and computing represented 22 percent. The advanced-products classification accounted for approximately 82 percent, but includes flip chip, memory, wafer-level processing, and related testing rather than only leading-edge AI packages. Current consolidated earnings therefore remain sensitive to mobile demand and other semiconductor markets. The Arizona thesis should be layered onto that diversified earnings base rather than used to reclassify the entire company as a pure AI infrastructure supplier. Amkor Technology

START-UP COSTS CAN OFFSET OPERATING IMPROVEMENT BEFORE ARIZONA REACHES SCALE

Management has identified approximately 100–200 basis points of operating-margin dilution beginning in 2027 from Arizona depreciation and start-up costs, with improvement expected in 2028. Preparation costs are expected to be recognized in operating expenses until programs qualify for production, after which they move into cost of goods sold. That accounting transition matters: a decline in start-up operating expense need not indicate that the economic burden has disappeared if the costs have migrated into gross margin. Amkor Technology

For scale, applying an annualized 100–200-basis-point impact to an illustrative $8 billion revenue base would imply $80 million to $160 million of operating-income pressure. At a 20 percent tax rate and 250 million diluted shares, that corresponds to approximately $0.26–$0.51 of EPS. This is a sensitivity calculation, not a 2027 earnings forecast; actual timing, revenue, tax rates, and qualification progress would determine the outcome.

The July call also explicitly identified underutilized Arizona manufacturing as a burden on both gross margin and operating margin in 2028. The additional development phase creates the possibility of overlapping investment and utilization ramps, in which the initial facility improves while subsequent capacity begins incurring costs. Shared infrastructure and accumulated operating experience may reduce the burden of the later phase, so mechanically doubling the initial start-up estimate would be inappropriate. Nevertheless, the expansion could extend the period before Arizona’s mature economics become visible in consolidated results. Amkor Technology

I used to build private equity diligence reports on data center sustainability, covering power, water, PUE, and capex risk in careful detail - but the human element was neglected and I imagine the same is case for the upcoming infra projects- like the largest data center planned for Pike County, Ohio. 

Pike County, Ohio has ~27,000 people and once powered American industry through uranium enrichment at the Portsmouth built in 1954.
 
But when the initial pump from the construction jobs building the uranium enrichment facility faded and even with a promised "community investment", Pikes County began to suffer until the plant finally closed in early 2020s leaving in it's wake:

- Median household income at ~$49k vs $70k for Ohio 
-  20% of residents living below the poverty line
- Labor force participation = ~51% vs 64% in Ohio.
- Overdose death rate at 61 per 100,000, vs 38 for Ohio.

Why can't data centers offer a more optimistic economic and cultural outcome

I will be forever proud of our school community for its response to the horror and tragedy of September 11, 2001.

I was teaching fifth grade at our little parish school, St. Joseph School in Randolph, Ohio. When it became clear what had happened, the whole school, grades K-8 children, teachers and staff went over to church to pray together.

In the following days, something very wonderful happened. Our students were able to offer hope and comfort to people affected by the events of September 11. Some moms came up with the idea of a video and one of the teachers was married to a videographer. One parent sang professionally.

The video featured the children praying and singing and offering words of comfort. The video (on VHS tape) was offered for free to anyone who requested it, only asking that they cover the postage. More than 600 copies were sent out across the country. Copies were delivered to fire and police stations in New York City. 

Just as the school reached out to comfort as many people as it could, many of the recipients of the videos wrote to thank the children and to let them know how much it meant to them.

I don’t have a copy of that video that I can post, but here’s a link to a feature local news did 10 years later. It gives just a little idea of what the video was like.

Mamas, Don’t Let Your Puppies Grow Up To Be Bitches

A puppy on the L-words is not cute. It is a training protocol. Love, light, law-of-attraction, “everyone is psychic,” phony Jesus with the edges sanded off — the hive that smiles until a trigger lands, then flips from hug to hunt without changing the slogan.

text:
< Be John Marshall
< Born 1755, a log cabin in Virginia's frontier
< First of fifteen children
< Your father surveys land for Lord Fairfax. You learn to read from Pope's Essay on Man.
< No formal schooling until you are fourteen
< At nineteen, the Revolution starts. You enlist.
< Valley Forge, 1777. You survive the winter that kills 2,000 men.
< You leave the Continental Army as a captain
< One year of law school at William & Mary. That is your entire legal education.
< You hang a shingle in Richmond. Clients come anyway.
< 1788, Virginia ratification convention. Patrick Henry wants to kill the Constitution.
< You argue for it. Virginia ratifies by ten votes.
< President Adams offers you a seat on the Supreme Court in 1798. You decline.
< He offers Secretary of State. You accept.
< January 1801, Adams is a lame duck. The Federalists are finished.
< Adams nominates you Chief Justice. The Senate confirms in one day.
< You are 45 years old
< The Court has no power. No building. No respect.
< Justices ride circuit like traveling salesmen
< Previous Chief Justices quit out of boredom
< 1803, Marbury v. Madison lands on your desk
< William Marbury wants his commission. You could order Jefferson to deliver it.
< You do something stranger. You say the law giving you that power is unconstitutional.
< Marbury loses. But now the Supreme Court decides what the Constitution means.
< You invented judicial review by pretending to lose
< Jefferson understands exactly what you did. He is furious for the rest of his life.
< You outlast him. You outlast Adams. You outlast every Founder who sits in the White House.
< 34 years as Chief Justice. You write 519 of the 1,106 decisions yourself.
< You create federal supremacy, contract law, the commerce clause
< You build the third branch of government with your bare hands
< July 6, 1835. You die in Philadelphia at eighty.
< The Liberty Bell cracks while tolling for your funeral
< Or so the story goes

The man who made the Supreme Court supreme had one year of legal training.

He never argued a case before the Court he would rule for three decades.

The Constitution does not mention judicial review anywhere. Marshall just wrote it in.

text:
1.  The Claim That Shocked Audiences: How Trump Told the Story and Shifted the Detail

Donald Trump repeatedly told audiences he had watched thousands of people in Jersey City celebrating as the Twin Towers collapsed; his phrasing and the story’s locus varied over time, sometimes citing supposed TV footage and at other times asserting he personally witnessed large crowds cheering in New Jersey. https://t.co/GLj0MkWUk9 and other reviewers documented that Trump’s account evolved and that he misquoted or misapplied contemporaneous reporting to support his version of events, turning unverified mentions into claims of mass celebration [2] [1]. The shifting narrative mattered to reviewers because verification hinges on consistent specifics—date, location, numbers, and source of the footage—and observers found that the particulars Trump offered did not match archived reporting or eyewitness testimony, undermining the credibility of the allegation [2] [3].

2. What National Fact-Checkers Concluded: Ratings, Evidence, and Methodology

Multiple national fact-checkers investigated and concluded the claim was false: PolitiFact rated the allegation “Pants on Fire,” and https://t.co/GLj0MkWUk9 gave the claim its harshest consideration, citing no evidence for thousands celebrating in New Jersey and noting that original reports either lacked verification or referred to isolated, unconfirmed incidents. These organizations compared Trump’s statements against contemporaneous news archives, statements from journalists who covered 9/11, and official records; they found no substantiation for the scale of celebration Trump described and flagged misattributed or misread sources as central errors

Donald Trump repeatedly told audiences he had watched thousands of people in Jersey City celebrating as the Twin Towers collapsed; his phrasing and the story’s locus varied over time, sometimes citing supposed TV footage and at other times asserting he personally witnessed large crowds cheering in New Jersey. https://t.co/GLj0MkWUk9 and other reviewers documented that Trump’s account evolved and that he misquoted or misapplied contemporaneous reporting to support his version of events, turning unverified mentions into claims of mass celebration [2] [1]. The shifting narrative mattered to reviewers because verification hinges on consistent specifics—date, location, numbers, and source of the footage—and observers found that the particulars Trump offered did not match archived reporting or eyewitness testimony, undermining the credibility of the allegation [2] [3].

2. What National Fact-Checkers Concluded: Ratings, Evidence, and Methodology

Multiple national fact-checkers investigated and concluded the claim was false: PolitiFact rated the allegation “Pants on Fire,” and https://t.co/GLj0MkWUk9 gave the claim its harshest consideration, citing no evidence for thousands celebrating in New Jersey and noting that original reports either lacked verification or referred to isolated, unconfirmed incidents. These organizations compared Trump’s statements against contemporaneous news archives, statements from journalists who covered 9/11, and official records; they found no substantiation for the scale of celebration Trump described and flagged misattributed or misread sources as central errors

1.  Eating balut eggs in Vietnam  
When I was in Vietnam, during my teenage years, I ate many DUCK BALUT EGGS.  Ducks were cheaper and more available, so were duck balut eggs.  We ate balut eggs with a mix of salt and pepper (and some tiny bit of sugar or MSG) and an herb called Vietnamese coriander.  When we break a balut egg, the first thing we would enjoy is the juice/broth inside the egg - THE MORE THE BETTER.  In extremely rare occasions, some of the duck balut eggs were not perfect or not good, and I could simply tell by the smell of the juice/broth inside the balut egg.  Yes, just the smell of the broth is how bad it could be.    

2.  Eating balut eggs in the USA  - A good experience
In the USA, I eat more of CHICKEN BALUT EGGS.  I buy balut egges at Pho Supplies in Zipcode 22041.  Chicken balut eggs are priced 3 for $1.25 while one duck balut egg costs $1.25.  So a duck balut egg costs three times a chicken balut egg.  I DO NOT BUY BALUT EGGS FROM GOOD FORTUNE SUPERMARKET BECAUSE THE PRICES FOR BALUT EGGS  THERE ARE HIGHER THAN PRICES AT Pho Supplies.  Pho Supplies receives ONE FRESH BATCH OF BALUT EGGS on Thursday each week.  So when I shop on Thursday, I get the most fresh eggs: inside each egg is a "living" young fetus of the chick.  The fetus is growing inside the balut egg.  If I buy the balut eggs on Saturday-Monday, the fetus inside could grow bigger, which builds a shape of a tiny bird with feather/hair.  So when we eat a balut egg with a young fetus, it tastes the most delicious; as the fetus grows inside the balut egg the next few days, the balut egg will taste less delicious as it develops soft bones and feather of a bird.  EVEN AFTER 5-6 DAYS FROM ARRIVAL AT THE STORE, THE BALUT EGG IS STILL CONSIDERED A GOOD EGG.  We can only say a balut egg is not good if the broth smells bad like rotten crabs.  But a grown chicken fetus does not indicate that this balut egg is disqualified for sale.  A balut egg is removed from sale if it is spoiled (has been out for many days, like more than a week or so, or rotten.  I also bought a few DUCK BALUT EGGS at Pho Supplies.  They also taste delicious like chicken balut eggs.  And once again, I tell if the duck balut egg is bad by its smell (of the broth inside the balut egg).

Incident A:  Unhappy Return and Refund Transaction

There was one incident in which I returned a 24-pk of Yeo's Sugar Cane Drink - Size 10.1 fl oz.  On the same day I bought, I opened the carton box and I gave away two (2) cans to a neighbor at my Mom's home.  Then my Mom and I consumed two cans.  We discovered that the drink tasted FLAT LIKE WATER WITH TABLE SUGAR although I did believe that at the factory, the manufacturer physically made the drink with real sugar cane and IT ADDED MORE TABLE SUGAR.  This information is on the Yeo's can.  

[Poor Taste + Bad Health Risk]
My Mom and I, we both have Diabetes Type 2.  So I could not figure out how we could consume the remaining 20 cans, knowing that the Yeo's sugar cane drink tastes like "sweet sugar water" and not anything like FRESH SUGAR CANE DRINK blended by the vendors on the streets of Vietnam.  (For the best taste, add a piece of kumquat).    

I will keep the story short and not go into every detail of the return transaction.  But the final response from the Front Store Manager was something like this:    

"I accept this return, but I will not accept one more time for a 24-pk of specialty drinks like Yeo's and other brands.  You should have tried one single-serve can of Yeo's Sugar Cane Drink first before you attempt to buy the 24-pk of Yeo's Sugar Cane Drink.  This will be our loss as we cannot sell the 20 cans from this carton box as single-serve cans.  Just 2-3 weeks ago, you also returned a 24-pk of Yeo's Lychee Drink.  So this is your second time returning the opened big 24-pk carton boxes."    

In her response, she made me feel as though SHE MADE A SPECIAL EXCEPTION FOR ME BECAUSE SHE HAD SEEN ME SHOPPING FREQUENTLY AS A REGULAR CUSTOMER.  I felt as though if I were not well-known to her, she could have REJECTED MY RETURN OF THE YEO'S SUGAR CANE DRINK.    

Here are the facts:  

1.  Yes, she was correct that just 2-3 weeks ago, I did return a 24-pk carton box of Yeo's Lychee Drink.  I DID OFFER TO PAY FOR THE CANS THAT I ALREADY CONSUMED, and the store only refunded me the difference, the value of the number of cans being returned.  The Yeo's Lychee Drink was simply FLAVORED LYCHEE DRINK (having just a hint of lychee) and it tasted FLAT LIKE SUGAR.  I have consumed LATIN AMERICAN LYCHEE DRINKS THAT TASTE DELICIOUS with a high concentration of juice content and lychee meat that I can bite on with my teeth.    

2.  For the Yeo's Sugar Cane Drink, I also did offer to pay for the cans that I already consumed and the store only credited me the value for the cans that I brought back.    

3.  I HAD NEVER SEEN A SINGLE-SERVE CAN OF YEO'S SUGAR CANE DRINK SOLD ANYWHERE PRIOR TO THE 24-PK PURCHASE AT GOOD FORTUNE SUPERMARKET.  Until today, I have not seen any single-serve or I have rarely seen a single-serve can of Yeo's Sugarcane Drink at any Vietnamese/Asian bakery shops or restaurants.  I have to say this because I cannot make a claim that "single-serve can" of Yeo's Sugar Cane Drink is not sold anywhere in Northern Virginia, where I live.

text:
It would have been too much for any of us to expect another bout to match what they had put on ten months earlier in Miami.

Alexis Arguello hits the canvas in the 4th round, courtesy of Aaron Pryor, on September 9, 1983, in the rematch of their epic battle in the Orange Bowl.

The rematch, held at Caesar's Palace in Las Vegas, will end with Pryor (in his 8th title defense) retaining his WBA Junior Welterweight Championship via 10th round KO.

Pryor floored Arguello three times: once in round one, once in the fourth, and for the count in the tenth. 

Arguello was counted out while sitting on the canvas with his arms draped around his knees.

Arguello was trained by Eddie Futch for his first fight with Pryor. He blamed Futch for the loss and fired him.

He would later apologize to Futch. "It was the biggest mistake of my life," Arguello would say of it. He was trained by Lupe Sanchez for the Pryor rematch.

Pryor was trained by Panama Lewis for his first fight with Arguello. Lewis had his license revoked after he had removed the padding from the gloves of Luis Resto before his fight with Billy Collins Jr. just two months prior to that fight. 

Pryor then hired Richie Giachetti to train him, but they had a falling out. Two weeks before the Arguello rematch, Pryor brought in Emanuel Steward as his trainer.

In hindsight, the suspicions of Lewis, and possible rule breaking in their magnificent first fight - not just the water bottle incident but Arguello's remarks to Futch that it felt like Pryor was hitting him with bricks - perhaps foreshadowing the crime committed against Collins at MSG - has hung over that first fight, the biggest win of Pryor's career, for decades. 

Luis Resto would later admit that Lewis had removed padding from his gloves for several fights and routinely gave his fighters an asthma medication, in their water bottles, that reportedly promoted rapid bursts of energy.  

It will always be a shame what Lewis did to the sport and, more tragically, to young Mr. Collins life.

Neither Pryor, nor Arguello, would ever be the same after this bout.

Arguello wouldn't fight for over two years following this loss, scoring TKO's over Pat Jefferson and Billy Costello, retiring only to return in 1994/95 splitting two decisions. 

Becoming involved in politics in his native country of Nicaragua, Arguello would die, some say suspiciously, in 2009 of what the regime there declared a "self-inflicted gunshot wound" though his family and friends dispute that to this day.

One of the most respected boxers of all-time, The Ring magazine named Arguello the greatest junior lightweight of all-time in 1994 and the eighth greatest featherweight of all-time and the twentieth best fighter of the last 80 years in 2002.

The Associated Press would name Arguello the best junior lightweight and the sixth best lightweight of the twentieth century in 1999.

In October of 1983, Pryor said he would not defend the WBA Junior Welterweight Championship against Johnny Bumphus, the #1-ranked contender, and sent the WBA a letter announcing his retirement. 

Robert Buechner, Pryor's attorney, said at the time, "I think that it's correct to say he would certainly reconsider his decision to retire if there's someone on the scene he thought had the same marketability and fighting ability he has." Officially, Pryor was stripped of the title. 

Pryor then announced in March of 1984 that he was ending his retirement. "I never really retired," he said. "I just rested." 

He successfully defended the Junior Welterweight Championship of the newly formed IBF twice before he was stripped of the title in December of 1985 due to inactivity.

Pryor was then out of boxing for 2 and 1/2 years due to drug and legal issues. 

A shell of his former self, he returned to the ring on August 8th of 1987, and was KO'd in seven rounds by Bobby Joe Young in the only defeat of his career.

Pryor then had trouble getting a boxing license late in his career because of eye problems. He underwent surgery on his left eye in January of 1988 to remove a cataract and repair a detached retina. Then he was declared legally blind in his left eye, with vision of 20/400. It improved to 20/70 with corrective lenses but he was denied a boxing license in Nevada, New York and California.

Prior to his first fight with Arguello, Aaron "Hawk" Pryor had seemed to inch towards one "Super-Fight" after another without any of them ever coming off as planned.

In December of 1980, Pryor had rejected an offer of $500,000 to fight Sugar Ray Leonard for the WBC Welterweight Championship because he wanted more money. When the amount was increased to $750,000, he rejected that as well.

Pryor then signed to fight WBC Super Lightweight Champion Saoul Mamby in a unification bout for $1 million. That bout was tentatively scheduled for February 7th of 1981. However, the fight fell apart when the promoter, Harold Smith, disappeared amid allegations that he was involved in a $21.3 million fraud against Wells Fargo National Bank. Smith, whose real name was Ross Fields, was later sentenced to ten years in prison after he was convicted of 29 counts of fraud and embezzlement. 

Pryor was then offered $750,000 to fight Roberto Duran at Madison Square Garden in April of 1981. 
Duran was fresh off of the "No Mas" debacle at that time. However, Pryor's new attorney told him not to sign anything until he worked out a new contract with his manager. By the time a new agreement had been worked out, the chance to fight Duran was gone (Duran would face Nino Gonzalez).

He then agreed to fight Leonard (not yet Arguello) in the fall of 1982 for $750,000, but Leonard first had to defend his welterweight title against Roger Stafford in Buffalo, New York, on May 14th of 1982. 

The Sunday before that bout, Pryor was driving to Buffalo from his Cincinnati home to taunt Leonard, to hype their planned bout, when he heard on his car radio the news that Leonard had suffered a detached retina in his left eye and the fight was off. 
Pryor would later say, "I pulled off to the side of the road and I cried."

The Ring named Pryor, who died in 2016 at the age of 60, the second greatest junior welterweight of all-time in 1994, and the Associated Press named him "Junior Welterweight Fighter of Century" in 1999.
